value_stream.name: Customer Mystery Shopping & Service Quality Assurance Program

fields.Participants: Service Quality, Store/Unit Leadership, CX (VS-13), HR (VS-103), Sales Enablement (VS-124)
fields.Volume: All service findings routed to units

Automation Opportunity: - Findings-routing workflow with SLA; corrective-action plan tracking; behavior-change confirmation via subsequent shops
Controls: - CTL-670 (ensure controlled execution — Findings Remediation, Recognition & Service-Quality Analytics (PA-146.3).)
- CTL-670: findings routed within SLA; corrective action verified & closed; behavior change confirmed
Cross-references: - links to VS-07 (store), VS-103 (HR), VS-124 (enablement), VS-13 (CX), W4376 (triage), W4378 (root-cause)
Pain Points / Risks: - **No-action risk**: findings acknowledged but not actioned → repeat failure; mitigated by closure verification & behavior-change confirmation
- **Feedback-delay risk**: slow feedback → lost learning moment; mitigated by feedback SLA
System Touchpoints: - Service-quality system (W4368); store ops (VS-07); HR (VS-103); sales enablement (VS-124); CX (VS-13)

steps.activity: Service Quality route findings to the responsible unit/store with evidence & score, within a feedback SLA (days)
Unit leadership acknowledge, plan corrective action (coaching, retraining, process fix), and execute within an agreed timeframe
Service Quality/HR verify corrective-action completion, confirm behavior change in subsequent shops, and close the finding

fields.Participants: Service Quality, OpEx (VS-133), CX (VS-13), Store Ops (VS-07), HR (VS-103), Strategy (VS-33)

workflows.name: Root-Cause Service Failure Analysis & Remediation Plan

Automation Opportunity: - Pattern detection across findings; root-cause analytics; remediation-impact tracking; standardization workflow
Controls: - CTL-670 (ensure controlled execution — Findings Remediation, Recognition & Service-Quality Analytics (PA-146.3).)
- CTL-670: systemic failures root-caused (VS-133); remediation addresses root cause; impact tracked & scaled
Cross-references: - links to VS-133 (OpEx), VS-13 (CX), VS-07 (store), VS-124 (training), VS-19.3 (WFM), W4377 (corrective action), W4384 (improvement)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Symptom-fix risk**: addressing symptoms not root cause → recurrence; mitigated by root-cause analysis (VS-133)
- **Scale-miss risk**: successful fix not standardized → inconsistent; mitigated by standardization/scaling
System Touchpoints: - Service-quality system (W4368); OpEx (VS-133); CX (VS-13); store ops (VS-07); HR (VS-103); strategy (VS-33)

steps.a: Head of Service Quality / OpEx Lead
steps.activity: Service Quality/OpEx identify patterns & systemic failures (repeated across stores/regions/associates), and run root-cause analysis (5-why, process VS-133)
Cross-functional team design the remediation plan (training VS-124, process redesign VS-133, staffing VS-19.3, tools, policy) addressing root cause
steps.r: Service Quality / OpEx / Store Ops / HR

steps.a: Head of Service Quality / OpEx Lead
steps.activity: Service Quality/OpEx track remediation impact on subsequent service scores, and standardize/scale successful fixes

fields.Participants: HR (VS-102/VS-103), Service Quality, Store Ops (VS-07), Finance (VS-17.4), CX (VS-13)

Automation Opportunity: - KPI-to-incentive auto-link; recognition workflow; ROI analytics; fairness/gaming monitoring
Controls: - CTL-670 (ensure controlled execution — Findings Remediation, Recognition & Service-Quality Analytics (PA-146.3).)
- CTL-670: incentive linked to validated KPI (W4364/W4375); integrity-controlled (W4381); balanced recognition; dispute path (W4380)
Cross-references: - links to VS-102/VS-103 (HR/comp), VS-17.4 (finance), VS-07 (store), W4364 (KPI), W4365 (ethics), W4375 (validation), W4381 (integrity)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Gaming-for-incentive risk**: incentive drives gamed behavior; mitigated by integrity controls (W4381) & validated scoring (W4375)
- **Demotivation risk**: punitive-only use → demotivation; mitigated by balanced recognition (positive + corrective)
System Touchpoints: - HR/comp (VS-102/VS-103); finance (VS-17.4); store ops (VS-07); CX (VS-13); service-quality system (W4368)

steps.activity: HR/Service Quality link service-quality KPI (W4364) to recognition/incentive (service-excellence awards, variable-pay component VS-102.3) within fairness/ethics (W4365)
HR/Store Ops administer recognition & incentive payouts based on validated scores (W4375), with the dispute path (W4380) available
Finance/HR track incentive cost vs service/CX outcome (ROI), and tune the incentive design

fields.Participants: Service Quality, HR (VS-103), Labor Relations (VS-84), Store Ops (VS-07), CX (VS-13)

Automation Opportunity: - Dispute-intake workflow; evidence re-validation; outcome-tracking; anti-retaliation monitoring
Controls: - CTL-670 (ensure controlled execution — Findings Remediation, Recognition & Service-Quality Analytics (PA-146.3).)
- CTL-670: dispute channel available; evidence re-validated; due process (W4365); anti-retaliation enforced
Cross-references: - links to VS-103 (HR), VS-84 (labor), VS-119 (ethics/anti-retaliation), W4365 (ethics), W4375 (validation), W4381 (integrity)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Unfair-finding risk**: erroneous finding harms associate; mitigated by re-validation & due process
- **Retaliation risk**: associate penalized for disputing; mitigated by anti-retaliation (W4365/VS-119)
System Touchpoints: - Service-quality system (W4368); HR (VS-103); labor relations (VS-84); CX (VS-13)

steps.activity: Associate/unit raise a dispute on a finding (factual error, context, fairness) via a defined channel within a window
Service Quality/HR re-validate the evidence (W4375), investigate context, and determine uphold/correct/withdraw with due process (W4365)
Service Quality/HR communicate outcome, adjust records/scores if corrected, and ensure no retaliation for disputing

fields.Participants: Service Quality, Audit (VS-21), Risk (VS-21.2), LP (VS-23), Vendor (VS-34), Ethics (VS-119)
fields.Trigger: Program operation; anomaly detected; audit cycle

Automation Opportunity: - Geo/time verification; duplicate/fabrication detection; gaming-pattern analytics; integrity-scorecard
Controls: - CTL-670 (ensure controlled execution — Findings Remediation, Recognition & Service-Quality Analytics (PA-146.3).)
- CTL-670: integrity controls (re-audit, evidence-verification, rotation); fraud/collusion investigated; suspect data quarantined; consequence enforced
Cross-references: - links to VS-21 (audit), VS-21.2 (risk), VS-23 (LP), VS-119 (ethics), W4363 (methodology), W4375 (QC), W4380 (dispute)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Fabrication risk**: fabricated shop reports → unreliable data & wrong decisions; mitigated by evidence-verification & re-audit
- **Collusion risk**: shopper-associate collusion → gamed scores; mitigated by rotation, no-notice, gaming detection
System Touchpoints: - Audit (VS-21); risk (VS-21.2); LP (VS-23); ethics (VS-119); vendor (VS-34); service-quality system (W4368)

steps.a: Audit Lead / Head of Service Quality
steps.activity: Audit/Service Quality define integrity controls — randomized re-audit, evidence-spot-check, geo/time verification, shopper rotation, duplicate/gaming detection, vendor-integrity SLA
Audit/LP monitor for fraud/collusion (fabricated visits, leaked schedules, shopper-associate collusion, score-manipulation), investigate anomalies, and quarantine suspect data (W4375)

steps.a: Head of Service Quality / Ethics Lead
steps.activity: Service Quality/Ethics enforce consequence on confirmed fraud/collusion (vendor penalty, shopper removal, associate action per due process W4380), and feed prevention

fields.Participants: Service Quality, BI (VS-28), Strategy (VS-33), CX (VS-13), Competitive Intel (VS-57/VS-33.3)

Automation Opportunity: - Trend/benchmark dashboards; service-CX-business-outcome correlation; competitive-tracking; improvement-prioritization analytics
Controls: - CTL-670 (ensure controlled execution — Findings Remediation, Recognition & Service-Quality Analytics (PA-146.3).)
- CTL-670: trends tracked & correlated to CX/outcomes; competitively benchmarked; insight fed to improvement
Cross-references: - links to VS-28 (BI), VS-13 (CX), VS-33/VS-57 (strategy/competitive), W4364 (KPI), W4378 (root-cause), W4384 (improvement)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Insight-isolation risk**: service data not linked to CX/business outcomes → low action; mitigated by correlation analytics
- **Benchmark-gap risk**: no competitive benchmark → blind to relative position; mitigated by competitive benchmarking
System Touchpoints: - BI (VS-28); CX (VS-13); strategy (VS-33); competitive intel (VS-57/VS-33.3); service-quality system (W4368)

steps.activity: Service Quality/BI track service-quality trends over time (store/region/touchpoint/KPI W4364), and correlate with CX/loyalty (VS-13) and business outcomes (conversion, repeat)
Strategy/Competitive Intel benchmark vs competitors (competitor mystery-shop/competitive intel VS-57/VS-33.3) and industry, identifying gaps/advantages
Service Quality/Strategy report trend/benchmark insight, and feed improvement prioritization (W4378/W4384)

fields.Frequency: Monthly to leadership + quarterly/annual to board
fields.Participants: Service Quality, CX (VS-13), Audit (VS-21), Leadership, Board (VS-36), Risk (VS-21.2)

workflows.name: Service-Quality Reporting to Leadership & Board Assurance

Automation Opportunity: - Auto-generated leadership/board reports; exception/critical-finding focus; assurance dashboard
Controls: - CTL-670 (ensure controlled execution — Findings Remediation, Recognition & Service-Quality Analytics (PA-146.3).)
- CTL-670: independent/integrity-controlled reporting; critical/systemic escalated; board assurance over control environment
Cross-references: - links to VS-13 (CX), VS-21 (audit), VS-36 (board), VS-21.2 (risk), W4364 (KPI), W4381 (integrity), W4382 (trend/benchmark)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Assurance-gap risk**: leadership lacks reliable service-quality assurance; mitigated by independent, integrity-controlled reporting
- **Reporting-overload risk**: too much detail → low action; mitigated by exception/critical-focused reporting
System Touchpoints: - Service-quality system (W4368); CX (VS-13); audit (VS-21); governance/board (VS-36); risk (VS-21.2)
Time Estimate: - Monthly report ~1–2 days; board view quarterly

steps.activity: Service Quality/CX prepare the leadership service-quality report (KPI trend W4364, critical findings, remediation progress, CX correlation)
Audit/Service Quality prepare the board-assurance view (program integrity W4381, independence W4365, systemic risk, regulatory/privacy W4367)
Leadership/Board review, direct action on systemic/critical issues, and confirm assurance over the service-quality control environment

fields.Participants: Service Quality, Strategy (VS-33), OpEx (VS-133), Finance (VS-17.4), CX (VS-13), HR (VS-103)

workflows.name: Service-Quality Program Maturity, ROI & Continuous Improvement

Controls: - CTL-670 (ensure controlled execution — Findings Remediation, Recognition & Service-Quality Analytics (PA-146.3).)
- CTL-670: program maturity assessed; ROI quantified; continuous improvement driven; investment prioritized
Cross-references: - links to VS-33 (strategy), VS-133 (OpEx), VS-17.4 (finance), VS-13 (CX), W4378 (root-cause), W4382 (trend), W4383 (reporting)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Low-ROI risk**: program cost exceeds service/CX value; mitigated by ROI quantification & prioritization
- **Stagnation risk**: methodology/coverage not evolving → diminishing value; mitigated by maturity assessment & continuous improvement
System Touchpoints: - Strategy (VS-33); OpEx (VS-133); finance (VS-17.4); CX (VS-13); HR (VS-103); service-quality system (W4368)

steps.activity: Service Quality/Strategy assess program maturity (coverage, methodology, integrity, action-effectiveness, analytics) vs a maturity model, and identify gaps
Finance/Service Quality quantify program ROI (service/CX improvement → conversion/repeat/retention value vs program cost incl agency)
Service Quality/OpEx drive continuous improvement (methodology, coverage, integrity, analytics, action-effectiveness), and prioritize investment
